headline: Charter Flight Access and Basecamp Reservations Required
reservation: Access to Ivvavik is primarily via chartered aircraft from Inuvik, as no road network enters the park. Visitors must coordinate with Parks Canada for basecamp stays at Imniarvik or register for independent backcountry travel; permit systems and availability change seasonally, so verify current status with the Inuvik office.

days.title: Arctic Watershed and Firth River Entry
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Inuvik via air charter

stops.name: Imniarvik Basecamp
stops.detail: Establish a base at this cultural site where visitors can learn about the Inuvialuit heritage of the British Mountains.

stops.name: Firth River
stops.detail: Observe the ancient canyon systems of one of the oldest rivers in North America, known for its pristine waters and Class IV rapids.

days.driving: Roughly 60-90 minutes by air; conditions vary significantly with weather.
days.note: All movement is subject to polar bear safety protocols and weather-dependent flight schedules.

days.title: Beringia Tundra Exploration

stops.name: Inspiration Point
stops.detail: Hike the ridges of the British Mountains, an unglaciated landscape that served as a refuge during the last ice age.

stops.name: Wolf Creek
stops.detail: Walk the valley floors to search for signs of the Porcupine Caribou Herd and local muskoxen populations.

days.driving: Local walking only; terrain varies by moisture levels.
days.note: High-latitude sun means constant daylight in mid-summer, making time management essential for rest.

days.title: Coastal Plain and Arctic Shoreline
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from Firth River camp

stops.name: Nunaluk Spit
stops.detail: Reach the edge of the Beaufort Sea where historical sod houses mark centuries of Inuvialuit occupation.

stops.name: Beaufort Sea Coast
stops.detail: Experience the contrast between the mountain foothills and the flat, bird-rich coastal wetlands.

days.driving: Allow time for local river transfer or charter repositioning.
days.note: Coastal fog can delay departures; keep flexible windows for return flights.

intel.title: Fly-in Operations
intel.text: Fixed-wing aircraft are the standard transport from Inuvik. Always confirm the weight limits for gear with your specific charter provider.

intel.title: Communication Realities
intel.text: Cellular service does not exist within the park boundaries. Satellite communication devices are the only reliable way to contact the Inuvik dispatch.

intel.title: Inuvik Logistics
intel.text: Final fuel and stove canister supplies must be secured in Inuvik before boarding your flight. There are no retail services available once you depart the airport.

intel.title: The Midnight Sun
intel.text: During the summer peak, the sun does not set, which can disrupt sleep cycles. Bring eye masks and monitor energy levels during long hiking days.

intel.title: Airport Long-term Lots
intel.text: Secure parking is located at the Mike Zubko Airport in Inuvik. Confirm duration limits with airport authorities if leaving a vehicle for multiple weeks.

plan.arrival: Upon landing at YEV, collect gear and finalize Inuvialuit land access registration at the Parks Canada office in Inuvik before your bush flight.
plan.vehicle: No road vehicles; air charter and walking are the only transit modes within Ivvavik.
plan.goldenHour: Inspiration Point offers dramatic light during the low-arc sun of late August.
